statement.p: Find the mass of the solid bounded by the xy-plane, yz-plane, xz-plane, and the plane (x/4)+(y/4)+(z/16) = 1, if the density of the solid is given by \delta (x,y,z)=x + 4 y.

static.solution:
z = 16 - 4 x - 4 y. Note that the projection of this into the xy-plane is the triangular region below y = 4 - x.
The mass of the volume is then M = \int_R \delta\,dV = \int_0^4\int_0^{4 - x}\int_0^{16-4 x-4 y}\,x + 4 y\,dz\,dy\,dx. Integrating with respect to z, M = \int_0^4\int_0^{4 - x} (x + 4 y)(16-4 x-4 y)\,dy\,dx so that M = \int_0^4\int_0^{4 - x} -4 x^2 + 16 x - 4 x y - 16 x y + 64 y - 16 y^2\,dy\,dx. Then, integrating with respect to y, M = \int_0^4 (-4 x^2 + 16 x)(4 - x) + \frac12(64 - 20 x)(4 - x)^2 - \frac{16}{3} (4 - x)^3\,dx. Expanding the these terms, we have M = \int_0^4 \frac{-2}{3} x^3 + 16 x^2 - 96 x + \frac{512}{3}\, dx = \frac{640}{3}.
